heroHeadline: SAC Airstrikes Kill PDF Fighters in Sagaing; AA Chief Opens Door to Talks — Day 1,939 as Junta Multi-Front Offensive Continues
heroSubtitle: On Day 1,939 of Myanmar's civil war (May 25, 2026), SAC jets struck Hman Hae Village in PDF-controlled Mawluu area, Indaw Township, Sagaing Region, killing five resistance fighters and injuring two civilians — part of the junta's ongoing effort to clear the PDF-held Indaw-Katha corridor following the recapture of the Mandalay-Myitkyina highway on May 5. In a rare diplomatic signal, Arakan Army Commander Twan Mrat Naing spoke to The Diplomat about openness to eventual talks with the Myanmar government and the AA's evolving relations with India and Bangladesh — reflecting the AA's growing political confidence as de facto ruler of 90% of Rakhine State, but also increasing international scrutiny following HRW's May 18 report documenting the AA's alleged May 2024 massacre of at least 170 Rohingya (including 90+ children) at Hoyyar Siri village, Buthidaung. The interview comes as Min Aung Hlaing's new civilian-facade government — inaugurated April 10, 2026 — conducts simultaneous offensives across Sagaing, Kachin, Rakhine, and Tanintharyi, while extending diplomatic outreach to the AA and TNLA in parallel. The KIA remains on tactical defensive since May 22, absorbing the SAC's 300-vehicle armored reinforcement convoy to Myitkyina — the largest junta Kachin deployment in years — while retaining all previously captured positions including the jade-mining corridor, the Hpakant-Karmaing road closure, and a 100-meter encirclement of Infantry Battalion 58 in Waingmaw. UN assessments document 16.2 million people — one-third of Myanmar's population — requiring humanitarian aid, with 12 million facing acute hunger in 2026.
